source: NEB Grade 12 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Two bags contain balls: Bag I has 3 red and 4 white balls, Bag II has 5 red and 6 white balls. A bag is chosen at random and a ball is drawn from it and found to be red. Find the probability that it came from Bag II.
questions.knowledgeNote: Bayes' theorem updates a prior by the likelihood; the normalising denominator (total probability) must be computed first and kept exact as a fraction.

questions.question: If P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.4 and A and B are independent, find P(A ∪ B) and P(A|B).
questions.solution:
Independence gives P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B) = 0.3 × 0.4 = 0.12.

**P(A ∪ B)** = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B) = 0.3 + 0.4 − 0.12 = **0.58**.

**P(A|B)** = P(A ∩ B)/P(B) = 0.12/0.4 = **0.3 = P(A)**, confirming independence (the occurrence of B does not change A's probability).
questions.knowledgeNote: Independent events satisfy P(A|B) = P(A); mutually exclusive events satisfy P(A ∩ B) = 0 — the two are frequently confused.

questions.question: A fair die is thrown 10 times. Find the mean and the variance of the number of times a six appears, and state the distribution used.
questions.solution:
Each throw is an independent Bernoulli trial with p = 1/6 (six) and q = 5/6, so the number of sixes X follows a **binomial distribution** with n = 10.

**Mean** = np = 10 × 1/6 = **5/3 ≈ 1.67**.

**Variance** = npq = 10 × (1/6) × (5/6) = 50/36 = **25/18 ≈ 1.39**, so the standard deviation is √(25/18) ≈ 1.18.
questions.knowledgeNote: Binomial conditions: fixed number of trials, two outcomes, constant p and independence — state them before applying mean np and variance npq.
